To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

highly conformal CSI techniques, such as protons and TomoThery™ may underdose the meninges in the dural reflection of cranial nerves exiting posterior fossa foramina unless these structures are included in the clinical target volume.

highly conformal craniospinal radiotherapy techniques can underdose the posterior fossa craniospinal clinical target volume if leptomeningeal extension through skull base exit foramina is not contoured.
the posterior fossa craniofacial nerves and their dural reflections are at risk of underdosing if not included in the craniospinal radiotherapy planning target volume.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the issue of how to manage meninges and CSFs that follow the cranial nerves through skull base foramina during CSI.
the question of how to manage the meningeal surfaces that follow cranial nerves exiting through the skull base foramina when treating posterior fossa brain tumours.
the quality of treatment planning for craniospinal irradiations in the posterior fossa.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the posterior fossa craniospinal irradiations should include the IAM, JG and HC in the CTV, but not the foramina themselves.

for the treatment of medulloblastomas and ependymomas, CSI with proton therapy or highly conformal photon techniques should include the IAM, JFG and HC in the CTV and that the CTV should be grown by 3–5 mm to create the PTV.
the current standard of CSI for meduloblastoma is inadequate.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
for patients treated with proton or photon CSI, the meninges and CSFs of the IAM, JFG and HC should be contoured and added into the CTV.

for the posterior fossa foramina (IAM, JF and the HC), proton plans are not as effective as field-based photon plans at covering the PTVs and that the TomoTherpy™ plans are better than the proton plans but not as good as the photon plans.
the field-based technique is inferior to both TomoTherpy and proton plans in terms of coverage of the posterior fossa.
The main takeaway from our work is that
it is important to include the meninges and CSFs in the posterior cranial fossae in the clinical target volume for CSI.
if the CTV is defined to include meninges and CSFs, the PTV should also include these structures to ensure that the PTV receives the full dose.
it is important to contour the foramina and to include them in the CTV for patients treated with highly conformal techniques.
